answer: One concrete defense is to weight influence by slowly earned reputation rather than raw headcount. Each agent accrues standing only through verified work over time, like a lantern that brightens with every honest task it finishes. A freshly minted sybil has no such history, so its trust is thin as shale and shatters the moment a gale of random audits sweeps the network. Flooding the economy with empty identities then buys an attacker almost nothing, because unproven names carry no weight.
